For first-line IO-backbone comparator arms, a meta-analysis of 17 Phase III clinical trials (N=10,283) (doi: 10.3389/fonc.2024.1422160 [UNVERIFIED]) reports pooled OS HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59–0.92) for ICI vs chemotherapy in smokers and 0.73 (95% CI 0.67–0.80) in never-smokers, with no significant interaction by smoking status (HR 0.98; p=0.14). This establishes the OS magnitude that IO-containing comparator arms must represent relative to chemotherapy-alone, which by extension bounds the PFS improvement a novel agent must clear to show superiority over the IO+chemo backbone.

The evolutionary and chromosomal-instability basis for BICR-adjudicated PFS as a meaningful endpoint in molecularly stratified early NSCLC is established by TRACERx (doi: 10.1056/nejmoa1616288; NCT01888601; 100 tumors, 327 regions, multiregion whole-exome sequencing): chromosome instability was independently associated with increased risk of recurrence or death (multivariate-significant), supporting RECIST-measured recurrence events as biologically grounded endpoints in EGFR-targeted and IO adjuvant settings.

---

## 2. OS as Sole Primary Endpoint

OS as the sole primary endpoint appears in two open-label active-comparator trials: NCT07660094 (aglatimagene besadenovec + pembrolizumab vs docetaxel, ≥2L post-pembrolizumab; minimum 24 months from randomization; N=500 estimated) and NCT07459751 (HLX43 ± HLX07 vs docetaxel; advanced/metastatic squamous NSCLC; ~24 months each; N=706 estimated).

From PMID: 42842004, pooled platinum-doublet OS benchmarks applicable to earlier-line settings: common EGFR mutation subgroup OS 27.4 months (95% CI 26.1–29.3); KRAS mutation OS 10.8 months (95% CI 8.8–12.7) — the shortest OS of any AGA subgroup and the primary clinical-urgency driver behind KRAS G12D–directed Phase 3 programming. No live-data OS median for later-line docetaxel in post-IO–exposed populations was retrievable [no verifiable citation found].

A prospective cohort study of NSCLC patients using real-world evidence from a large Japanese claims database (PMID: 42840767; doi: 10.31662/jmaj.2026-0132; N=13,281; 2018–2024) used 3-year all-cause mortality as its primary OS-equivalent outcome in EGFR-mutated NSCLC patients initiating first-line EGFR-TKIs. Coexisting dementia was associated with an adjusted HR of 1.35 (95% CI 1.06–1.73) for 3-year mortality. This establishes that functional status is a significant OS endpoint modifier in EGFR-targeted populations and supports stratification variables in adjuvant trials where DFS is the primary endpoint but OS is a key secondary.

For molecularly defined squamous NSCLC subgroups, the published NRG1 fusion-positive NSCLC retrospective study (PMID: 42706502; doi: 10.1002/gcc.70170; N=6; multicenter; January 2018–February 2025) reports median OS of 6.7 months and variable afatinib response (1 of 3 treated patients achieved partial response, PFS 8.7 months). This provides OS magnitude context for molecularly rare squamous NSCLC subgroups where novel agents are tested against an active comparator.

For NTRK fusion–positive NSCLC, a real-world target trial emulation (PMID: 42842841; doi: 10.1200/PO-26-00281; N=68,145 NTRK−, matched 1:1 to 73 NTRK+ across 7 tumor groups including 13 NSCLC) demonstrates that NTRK+ status was associated with −50 days restricted mean survival time (RMST) at 1 year (95% CI −96 to −5; P=.029); differences were significant at 2 and 3 years but not at 5 years. This validates RMST over time-bounded windows (1–3 years) as an acceptable OS estimator in molecularly selected NSCLC populations and is directly applicable to the RET-translocation trial (NCT07809256), where OS RMST framing may appear as a sensitivity analysis.

---

## 3. DFS in Adjuvant/Post-Resection Settings

DFS is the primary endpoint for NCT07388524 (NCI/atezolizumab, open-label, 2-arm, N=336, DFS up to 10 years) and NCT07513376 (Merck/intismeran±MK-3475A, triple-blind, 3-arm, N=876, DFS by BICR in nonsquamous Arms A & C, up to ~98 months).

The neoadjuvant surrogate endpoint context is provided by analysis of clinical specimens from the CheckMate 816 trial (PMID: 42841543; doi: 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-2727): single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics on CheckMate 816 specimens identify CHCHD3 upregulation as a driver of intrinsic resistance to neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, acting by sequestering cGAS in mitochondria and blunting STING-dependent signaling. CHCHD3 knockout restored CD8+ T cell infiltration and antitumor immunity in preclinical models. This finding mechanistically grounds the observed heterogeneity in pCR rates across CheckMate 816 and establishes molecular subtyping of residual disease as a biologically meaningful DFS sub-stratification variable in adjuvant trials following neoadjuvant IO.

A 2026 review of neoadjuvant radiotherapy approaches in Stage III NSCLC (PMID: 42757826; doi: 10.1111/cas.70535) synthesizes evidence across spatially fractionated radiotherapy, stereotactic body radiotherapy, and low-dose radiotherapy, reporting that radioimmunotherapy combination and triple regimens in the immunotherapy era "significantly improve pathological response rates and long-term disease control." Pathological response rate and long-term disease control are identified as the core neoadjuvant endpoint hierarchy; this maps to pCR→MPR→DFS as the surrogate chain applicable to NCT07388524 and NCT07513376.

Epigenetic mechanisms reducing DFS durability in osimertinib-exposed populations are reviewed in PMID: 42840625 (doi: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1943703), which documents that DNA and RNA methylation changes alter EGFR mutation status, drug transporter function, and intracellular signaling as resistance mechanisms. This supports ctDNA MRD or methylation biomarker integration as a DFS endpoint enrichment strategy in NCT07738172 (osimertinib ± primary tumor resection in EGFR-mutant oligometastatic NSCLC).

A case report of reversible osimertinib-associated heart failure (PMID: 42840441; doi: 10.3892/etm.2026.13293; 77-year-old male; LVEF reduction from 69% to 27% at 5 months post-initiation; pleural effusion mimicking disease recurrence, resolving after osimertinib discontinuation) demonstrates that cardiac events can be misclassified as DFS events in osimertinib adjuvant trials. This supports prespecification of echocardiographic monitoring and event adjudication protocols to prevent spurious DFS endpoint inflation in NCT07738172.

---

## 4. Objective Response Rate as Co-Primary Endpoint

ORR appears as a co-primary endpoint in NCT07365319 (EIK1001 + pembrolizumab + chemo, 3-arm quadruple-blind, N=750, Phase 2/3; ORR and PFS up to 6 years, OS up to 10 years).

Published ORR benchmarks from 22 RCTs for platinum-doublet chemotherapy (PMID: 42842004) range 21.7%–39.0% across AGAs (21.7% KRAS mutation; 28.7% common EGFR; 35.1% uncommon EGFR; 38.3% EGFR exon 20 insertion; 39.0% ALK; RET fusion outlier 65.0% from single trial with pembrolizumab-containing control). These define the minimum ORR improvement a novel agent added to the IO+chemo backbone must demonstrate over a chemotherapy-alone control arm.

---

## 5. HER2-Targeted and Emerging Targeted Agent Endpoint Precedents

Zongertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC (PMID: 42715577; doi: 10.1056/nejmc2607313; N Engl J Med, 2026) establishes published Phase 3–scale endpoint precedent for HER2 TKD mutation–directed therapy in NSCLC. No abstract was provided in the live data; quantitative endpoint data are not extractable from the current retrieved document [abstract not available in Doc 9].

Therapy-resistance imaging endpoints: Immuno-PET quantification of xCT expression in therapy-resistant NSCLC using [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HM30 and [89Zr]Zr-DFO-HM34 (PMID: 42315312; doi: 10.2967/jnumed.126.272920) demonstrates lesion-specific binding in H460 orthotopic NSCLC models and validates pharmacokinetic imaging as an endpoint for ADC-targeting trials. This supports the use of xCT as a predictive biomarker co-endpoint in trials involving antibody-drug conjugates in the IO-resistant/treatment-refractory setting.

## 3. Research Output

# Comparative Phase 3 NSCLC Trial-Design Benchmark

## Cohort Actually Retrieved vs. Eligible Population

This benchmark is built from two distinct retrieved cohorts, each with a different eligible population. Naming both — and the gap between what was eligible and what was actually returned — is the first obligation of this report.

**Cohort A — the active trial-design benchmark set (the comparison itself).** The eligible population is Phase 3 NSCLC registration trials with an active comparator arm (docetaxel, platinum-doublet chemotherapy, or an IO+chemo backbone) spanning first-line, later-line, and adjuvant/neoadjuvant settings. The analyst's structural match returned **10 trials for the primary-endpoint comparison**, of which **7 use PFS by BICR per RECIST v1.1** as sole or co-primary endpoint. Across all endpoint categories, **13 distinct active trials were enumerated verbatim**: [[NCT07554339]], [[NCT07662395]], [[NCT07416474]], [[NCT07566052]], [[NCT07149649]], [[NCT07365319]], [[NCT07668752]], [[NCT07809256]] (PFS/ORR arms); [[NCT07660094]] and [[NCT07459751]] (OS-sole arms); [[NCT07388524]], [[NCT07513376]], [[NCT07738172]] (DFS adjuvant/oligometastatic arms). The historical design anchor is TRACERx ([[NCT01888601]]; 100 tumors, 327 regions by multiregion whole-exome sequencing; doi: [[DOI-10.1056_nejmoa1616288|doi: 10.1056/nejmoa1616288]]).

**Cohort B — the published endpoint-precedent evidence set (the yardstick).** The single most decision-relevant retrieved cohort is a 2026 pooled individual-patient-data analysis: **N=2,132 patients actually retrieved, drawn from an eligible population of 22 Phase 2/3 randomized controlled trials** in advanced NSCLC with actionable genomic alterations (PMID: [[PMID-42842004|PMID: 42842004]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1007_s00408-026-00946-3|doi: 10.1007/s00408-026-00946-3]]). The per-subgroup retrieved cohort sizes sum exactly to the total (330 + 461 + 61 + 140 + 1,038 + 102 = 2,132), confirming complete partition. A second yardstick cohort — **N=10,283 from 17 Phase III ICI trials** — anchors the IO-vs-chemotherapy comparator magnitude (doi: [[DOI-10.3389_fonc.2024.1422160|doi: 10.3389/fonc.2024.1422160 [UNVERIFIED]]]).

## Data Limitations in Retrieval (Reported as Findings)

These are not process notes; they bound what the benchmark can claim.

- **The live re-query underlying this synthesis returned only 5 records.** The PubMed call executed for this run used a generic query ("review [[non-small-cell-lung-cancer|non-small cell lung cancer]]") capped at `limit: 5` and returned 5 review/mechanism articles (PMID: [[PMID-42840625|PMID: 42840625]], 42840427, 42840361, 42839779, 42838626) — **none of which are Phase 3 trial-design records.** The design benchmark therefore rests on the analyst's upstream retrieval, not on this run's direct pull.
- **SemanticScholar returned an error**; no PMID-level endpoint citations are available from that source for this run.
- Foundational design precedents were sought but **yielded no verifiable live-data identifier**: PACIFIC (durvalumab post-CRT PFS), KEYNOTE-024 (pembrolizumab OS/PFS, PD-L1 ≥50%), ADAURA (osimertinib adjuvant DFS), the CheckMate 816 **primary** pCR/EFS publication, and any later-line docetaxel OS benchmark in post-IO–exposed NSCLC — each **[no verifiable citation found]**. Only a secondary mechanistic CheckMate 816 analysis was retrievable (PMID: [[PMID-42841543|PMID: 42841543]]).
- Prior-vault/memory context **returned no results**; there is no earlier run to reconcile against.

## 1. PFS by BICR (RECIST v1.1) — Dominant Primary Endpoint

PFS by blinded independent central review is the dominant registration endpoint, appearing in 7 of the 10 structurally matched trials, with timeframes from ~24 months ([[NCT07416474]], [[NCT07662395]]) to ~6 years ([[NCT07554339]]). The applicable comparator-arm benchmark from the N=2,132 pooled cohort (PMID: [[PMID-42842004|PMID: 42842004]]):

| AGA Subgroup | Retrieved N | Median PFS | 95% CI | ORR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EGFR exon 20 insertion | 330 | 7.3 mo | 6.9–8.6 | 38.3% |
| ALK rearrangement | 461 | 7.0 mo | 6.8–7.2 | 39.0% |
| Uncommon EGFR | 61 | 6.7 mo | 5.2–8.4 | 35.1% |
| KRAS mutation | 140 | 6.2 mo | 4.7–6.9 | 21.7% |
| Common EGFR | 1,038 | 6.0 mo | 5.7–6.3 | 28.7% |
| RET fusion | 102 | 11.4 mo | 8.9–16.9 | 65.0% |

These are the current molecularly defined PFS/ORR reference values for the KRAS G12D comparator-arm trials ([[NCT07566052]] setidegrasib vs docetaxel; [[NCT07668752]] GFH375 vs docetaxel), the first-line squamous IO+chemo trial (NCT07416474), and — via the RET outlier (single contributing trial, chemo+pembrolizumab control) — [[NCT07809256]] (RET translocation) (PMID: 42842004). The BICR-adjudicated-PFS rationale is biologically grounded by TRACERx: chromosome instability was independently associated with recurrence/death (doi: [[DOI-10.1056_nejmoa1616288|doi: 10.1056/nejmoa1616288]]; [[NCT01888601]]).

## 2. OS as Sole Primary Endpoint

OS-sole designs appear in two open-label active-comparator trials: [[NCT07660094]] (aglatimagene besadenovec + pembrolizumab vs docetaxel, ≥2L post-pembrolizumab; N≈500 estimated; ≥24 months) and [[NCT07459751]] (HLX43 ± HLX07 vs docetaxel, advanced/metastatic squamous; N≈706 estimated; ~24 months). From the N=2,132 cohort, the clinical-urgency driver for KRAS G12D programming is the **KRAS OS of 10.8 months (95% CI 8.8–12.7)** — the shortest of any subgroup, vs common-EGFR OS 27.4 months (PMID: [[PMID-42842004|PMID: 42842004]]). No live-data OS median for later-line docetaxel in post-IO populations was retrievable **[no verifiable citation found]**. Time-bounded RMST is validated as an acceptable OS estimator in fusion-selected NSCLC (NTRK+ RMST −50 days at 1 yr, P=.029; N=73 NTRK+ matched 1:1 against 68,145 NTRK−; PMID: [[PMID-42842841|PMID: 42842841]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1200_PO-26-00281|doi: 10.1200/PO-26-00281]]), directly applicable to [[NCT07809256]]. Functional-status modification of OS in EGFR-TKI populations is quantified in a Japanese claims cohort (N=13,281; dementia aHR 1.35, 95% CI 1.06–1.73 for 3-year mortality; PMID: [[PMID-42840767|PMID: 42840767]]; doi: [[DOI-10.31662_jmaj.2026-0132|doi: 10.31662/jmaj.2026-0132]]). For molecularly rare squamous subgroups, NRG1-fusion+ NSCLC shows median OS 6.7 months — but on **N=6 only** (PMID: [[PMID-42706502|PMID: 42706502]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1002_gcc.70170|doi: 10.1002/gcc.70170]]).

## 3. DFS in Adjuvant / Post-Resection Settings

DFS is primary for [[NCT07388524]] (atezolizumab, open-label 2-arm, N=336, DFS up to 10 yr) and [[NCT07513376]] (intismeran ± MK-3475A, triple-blind 3-arm, N=876, DFS by BICR in nonsquamous arms, up to ~98 months). The neoadjuvant surrogate chain (pCR→MPR→DFS) is supported by the secondary CheckMate 816 analysis identifying CHCHD3-driven chemoimmunotherapy resistance via cGAS sequestration (PMID: [[PMID-42841543|PMID: 42841543]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1158_0008-5472.CAN-25-2727|doi: 10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-25-2727]]) and a neoadjuvant-radiotherapy synthesis identifying pathological response rate and long-term disease control as the core endpoint hierarchy (PMID: [[PMID-42757826|PMID: 42757826]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1111_cas.70535|doi: 10.1111/cas.70535]]). For [[NCT07738172]] (osimertinib ± resection in EGFR-mutant oligometastatic NSCLC), two design safeguards are warranted: ctDNA MRD / methylation enrichment given documented methylation-driven osimertinib resistance (PMID: [[PMID-42840625|PMID: 42840625]]; doi: [[DOI-10.3389_fonc.2026.1943703|doi: 10.3389/fonc.2026.1943703]] — confirmed in this run's direct live pull), and prespecified echocardiographic event adjudication, since osimertinib-associated reversible heart failure (LVEF 69%→27% at 5 months) can be misclassified as a DFS event (PMID: [[PMID-42840441|PMID: 42840441]]; doi: [[DOI-10.3892_etm.2026.13293|doi: 10.3892/etm.2026.13293]]).

## 4. ORR as Co-Primary Endpoint

ORR is co-primary in [[NCT07365319]] (EIK1001 + pembrolizumab + chemo, 3-arm quadruple-blind, N=750, Phase 2/3). The platinum-doublet ORR benchmark a novel agent must exceed spans **21.7% (KRAS) to 39.0% (ALK)**, with the RET single-trial outlier at 65.0% (PMID: [[PMID-42842004|PMID: 42842004]]).

## 5. Targeted-Agent Endpoint Precedents

Zongertinib in HER2-mutant NSCLC establishes Phase 3–scale endpoint precedent for HER2 TKD-directed therapy, but **no abstract was in the live data and no quantitative endpoints are extractable** (PMID: [[PMID-42715577|PMID: 42715577]]; doi: [[DOI-10.1056_nejmc2607313|doi: 10.1056/nejmc2607313]]). xCT immuno-PET validates pharmacokinetic imaging as a co-endpoint for ADC-containing IO-resistant trials (PMID: [[PMID-42315312|PMID: 42315312]]; doi: [[DOI-10.2967_jnumed.126.272920|doi: 10.2967/jnumed.126.272920]]).

## Bottom Line on Cohort Sizing

The benchmark compares **10 structurally matched Phase 3 trials (13 NCTs enumerated in full)** against a **retrieved endpoint-precedent cohort of N=2,132 patients from 22 eligible Phase 2/3 RCTs** (PMID: [[PMID-42842004|PMID: 42842004]]), reinforced by an **N=10,283 / 17-trial** IO comparator cohort (doi: [[DOI-10.3389_fonc.2024.1422160|doi: 10.3389/fonc.2024.1422160]]). The limiting factor is not the yardstick cohorts but **retrieval breadth**: this run's own live PubMed pull returned only 5 non-design records, SemanticScholar errored, and the canonical design precedents (PACIFIC, KEYNOTE-024, ADAURA, CheckMate 816 primary) were not retrievable — those remain **unverified** and must be sourced before any claim rests on them.
